claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct: detik means a second, one-sixtieth of a minute, in Indonesian.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: detik

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct: Malaysian Malay saat is an established term for a second; official Malaysian terminology defines 60 saat as one minute.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer: saat

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct: “second” and “unit of time shorter than a minute” match both answers in the intended measurement sense.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: Needs correction: different-common-word may imply exclusive national ownership. Use or annotate it as a shared synonym with Indonesian/Malaysian preference; no false-friend contrast is present.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation and false-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both translations and the English sense are correct, but the relation “different-common-word” is too categorical. Indonesian detik and Malaysian saat are standard terms for a second, while detik also occurs in Malaysian Malay and saat can refer more broadly to a moment. Teach this as a common national preference, not an exclusive contrast; there is no false-friend contrast.
